## Sync types and the velocity frame at seams (`type`) {#sec-ch03-synctype}

The stage update exchanges conserved variables, `hydro_u` and `scalar_s`, and rebuilds the scalar primitive from them
afterwards; the initial sync exchanges primitives, `hydro_w` and `scalar_r`. The face-state syncs carry primitive face
states (@sec-ch03-cslrsync) and the donor factor is a scalar (@sec-ch03-thetacopy). On a slab or cubed layout the type
does not matter, because a copy needs no rotation. On the cubed sphere the velocity of a strip is rotated to the global
spherical frame before it leaves the sender and into the receiver's panel frame after it lands; the type decides
whether the metric is applied around that rotation.

Local symbols: $\mathsf M$ the $3\times3$ pointwise matrix that takes a panel velocity to the
global spherical frame at one ghost position [-]; $\mathsf G$ the lowering of @eq-ch03-gnomonic-lower on $(v_2, v_3)$ [-]; $\mathsf R$[^rg-13ee58137cf2] the panel-to-spherical rotation [-].

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Say which variables each sync carries and how velocities cross a cubed-sphere panel edge: conserved
momenta covariant (raised, rotated, lowered), primitive velocities contravariant (rotated), scalars not rotated
(@eq-ch03-synctype-matrix).

**Data.** In/out: ghost strips of conserved, primitive or scalar variables, in their own units; the per-ghost
matrix [-].

**Placement.** Every sync across a panel edge.

**Activation.** `SyncOptions.type` (`kConserved`, `kPrimitive`, `kScalar`); default `kConserved`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact up to round-off (a change of basis), away from a pole.

**Evidence.** `test_coordinate`, `test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange_python`; check `[C14]`; the ctest
entries were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).
:::

### Derivation

The panel frame's velocity components are contravariant along the unit tangent vectors; the conserved momenta are
stored covariant (@eq-ch03-gnomonic-lower). The rotation to the spherical frame is defined on contravariant
components, through Cartesian components on the sphere. For a conserved strip the sender therefore raises first and
the receiver lowers last, and the code folds both into one matrix per ghost position:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf M^{\to\mathrm{sph}} &= \mathsf R^{\mathrm{sph}\leftarrow\mathrm{panel}}\,\mathsf G^{-1}, \\
\mathsf M^{\to\mathrm{panel}} &= \mathsf G\,\mathsf R^{\mathrm{panel}\leftarrow\mathrm{sph}},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-synctype-matrix}

with $\mathsf G$ the lowering of @eq-ch03-gnomonic-lower acting on $(v_2, v_3)$ and $\mathsf R$ the panel-to-spherical
map. A panel velocity with contravariant components $(v_1, v_2, v_3)$ is the vector
$\mathbf v = v_1\hat{\mathbf u} + v_2\hat{\mathbf t}_\xi + v_3\hat{\mathbf t}_\eta$, with the unit vectors of
@sec-ch03-gnomonic: $\hat{\mathbf u} = (1, X, Y)/Q$, $\hat{\mathbf t}_\xi = (-X, D^2, -XY)/(DQ)$ and
$\hat{\mathbf t}_\eta = (-Y, -XY, C^2)/(CQ)$ in the panel's own axes, which a fixed permutation and sign per panel turns
into global Cartesian axes. Its spherical components are its projections on
$(\hat{\mathbf e}_r, \hat{\mathbf e}_\theta, \hat{\mathbf e}_\varphi)$, so

$$
\mathsf R^{\mathrm{sph}\leftarrow\mathrm{panel}}_{ab} = \hat{\mathbf e}_a\cdot\hat{\mathbf t}_b, \qquad
\hat{\mathbf t}_1 = \hat{\mathbf u},\ \hat{\mathbf t}_2 = \hat{\mathbf t}_\xi,\ \hat{\mathbf t}_3 = \hat{\mathbf t}_\eta,
$$

with $\hat{\mathbf e}_r = \hat{\mathbf u}$, $\theta$ the colatitude and $\varphi$ the longitude of the point. The tangents are not
orthogonal, so $\mathsf R^{\mathrm{panel}\leftarrow\mathrm{sph}}$ is the inverse, not the transpose: it projects on the dual
vectors, $v_2 = (D/Q)(v_x - Xv_z)$ and $v_3 = (C/Q)(v_y - Yv_z)$, with $v_z$ the component along the panel normal
(the first axis of $\hat{\mathbf u} = (1, X, Y)/Q$) and $v_x, v_y$ the components along the two in-panel axes, as the
code names them. These are `cs_contra_to_cart_` and
`cs_cart_to_contra_` ({{< code src/coord/cubed_sphere_utils.cpp cs_contra_to_cart_ >}},
{{< code src/coord/cubed_sphere_utils.cpp cs_cart_to_contra_ >}}), composed with the Cartesian-to-spherical projection in
`cs_contra_to_sph_` ({{< code src/coord/cubed_sphere_utils.cpp cs_contra_to_sph_ >}}). For a primitive strip $\mathsf G$ is
left out. `cs_velocity_transform_matrix` builds each matrix numerically, column by column, by passing the three unit
vectors through these maps ({{< code src/coord/cubed_sphere_utils.cpp cs_velocity_transform_matrix >}}).
Each factor is exact; the composition is a change of basis and loses nothing but round-off. The check
builds $\mathsf G$ from the gnomonic angle at four ghost positions and $\mathsf R$ at four rotation angles and
forms both matrices of @eq-ch03-synctype-matrix: the round trip
$\mathsf M^{\to\mathrm{panel}}\mathsf M^{\to\mathrm{sph}}$ departs from the identity by round-off only, for the
conserved and for the primitive strip, which leaves $\mathsf G$ out, within the check's threshold, and
$\det\mathsf G - \sin^2\psi$ (with $\sin\psi$ the panel metric `sine_cell_kj` of @sec-ch03-gnomonic) is exactly zero, so $\mathsf G$ is invertible away from a pole (`[C14]`).[^st-c14]

[^st-c14]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C14]`; a numpy port of `cs_velocity_transform_matrix` at the pin, CPU, double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0. The two round-trip deviations
    are round-off of a few products of order-one entries and are read against the check's threshold, not as
    values.

### Numerical method

The matrix depends only on the angular position, so it is built for one radial plane and broadcast along $x_1$, and it
is cached per sync options, buffer, direction and shape (`_velocity_transform`). In the pack the rotation to the
spherical frame acts on the whole packed strip, margin included, before relabelling; in the unpack the rotation back acts only on the narrow
ghost zone after interpolation. The scalar primitive of the stage sync is rebuilt by `set_scalar_primitive` after the
exchange and the corner refresh. @tbl-ch03-synctype-calls lists the syncs.

| sync | type | interpolate | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| stage hydro / scalar | conserved / scalar | yes | `exchange_ghost_zones` |
| initial hydro / scalar | primitive / scalar | yes | `initialize` |
| face states | primitive, scalar | no | @sec-ch03-cslrsync |
| donor factor | scalar | no | @sec-ch03-thetacopy |
| `Mesh` level | caller's choice | yes | `Mesh::exchange_ghost_zones` |

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| stage sync, scalar rebuild | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}} | `set_scalar_primitive` | none |
| initial sync | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize >}} | `kPrimitive` | none |
| initial sync under `Mesh` | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize_under_mesh >}} | `initialize_under_mesh` | none |
| `Mesh`-level sync | {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}} | `exchange_ghost_zones` | `type` |
| matrix with raise or lower | {{< code src/coord/cubed_sphere_utils.cpp cs_velocity_transform_matrix >}} | `cs_velocity_transform_matrix` | `type` |
| cached matrix, one radial plane | {{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::_velocity_transform >}} | `_velocity_transform` | `type` |
| pack rotation | {{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::serialize >}} | `kConserved` | `type` |
| unpack rotation | {{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::deserialize >}} | `kPrimitive` | `type` |

: Code map of the sync types. {#tbl-ch03-synctype-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-synctype-code):

1. The caller picks the type in `SyncOptions`; `_velocity_transform` passes the cosine to the matrix only for
   `kConserved` ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::_velocity_transform >}}).
2. `serialize` applies `cs_apply_velocity_transform_` to the velocity rows of a conserved or primitive strip
   ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::serialize >}}); `deserialize` applies the inverse matrix with
   `cs_apply_velocity_transform_` ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::deserialize >}}).

**How to use it.** No YAML key: each caller sets `SyncOptions.type` in C++ (@tbl-ch03-synctype-calls); a
`Mesh`-level sync from Python takes the caller's type. The stage sync sets conserved, then scalar
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}):

```cpp
  SyncOptions sync_opts;
  sync_opts.interpolate(true).type(kConserved);
    ...
  if (pscalar->nvar() > 0) {
    sync_opts.type(kScalar);
    sync_vars.clear();
    sync_vars["scalar_s"] = scalar_s;
    exchange(sync_vars, sync_opts);
```

Nothing is refused; a primitive strip simply skips $\mathsf G$ in @eq-ch03-synctype-matrix.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_coordinate` | the cached matrices, with and without the metric, equal the direct transforms | $10^{-4}$ rel., $10^{-5}$ abs. | float32 cases |
| `test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange_python` | a radial velocity crosses every edge unchanged | $10^{-12}$ | @sec-ch03-exchange |

: Tests of the sync types. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-synctype-tests}

The matrix case is `cached_cubed_sphere_velocity_matrices_match_direct` ({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp DeviceTest.cached_cubed_sphere_velocity_matrices_match_direct >}}); it
runs on CPU and CUDA in float32 and float64 through `DeviceTest`. They were not run for this chapter at the pin
(missing evidence).

### Limits

No known limits. A tangential velocity crossing an edge is not tested end to end; only the radial component is (not
measured). The switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
